turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let me know if I am too quiet.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: You are fine, thank you for asking.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: What brings you to the clinic today?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Something is wrong with my chest, I think.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: When did you first notice it?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: This morning, while I was making tea.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Does it move into your arms or up toward your neck?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I feel it in my jaw sometimes.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: What kind of sensation is it?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My niece sent me a card, it has a picture of a bird on it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Does doing chores around the house set it off?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, when I carry the laundry.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Does anything ease the pain when it is there?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I took an antacid and it did not do anything.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Have you blacked out at all?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Is your breathing affected?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No trouble breathing at all.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let me ask about risk factors: tobacco, blood pressure, diabetes, cholesterol.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I have an irregular heartbeat. I have never smoked.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Has a parent or sibling had a heart attack?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My brother had bypass surgery.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Do you have a history of heart surgery or stents?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Nothing like that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: What are you taking at home for your health?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I take Apixaban.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let us wrap up with the plan. First, take one baby aspirin every morning. Second, call 911 if the pain gets worse or does not stop. To be sure I was clear, what will you do next?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I will take one baby aspirin each morning and call 911 if the pain gets worse or will not stop.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Anything else on your mind?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My daughter lives far away. I am afraid to be alone if this happens again.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: All right, we are done. Take care of yourself.
